# Σ-GLYPH

> A portable check engine: send a computation by hash, get the same answer on any
> machine, with work and memory bounded up front.
> `Receipt = eval(term_hash, atp: uint32, content_environment)` — deterministic,
> integer-only, total over its canonical exits. No float, no clock, no network.
> If the budget runs out, or demanded content is missing, that outcome is
> deterministic too.

Why anyone needs that: it lets you re-run a **stranger's** reason. A reviewer
re-executes a computation on their own laptop instead of trusting the log of
whoever wrote it. Bounding work *and* memory in advance is what makes running a
stranger's computation safe by construction.

This repository keeps two things: **Book I** (the compute core) and
**sigma-resume** (a long computation in budgeted segments, resumed from
checkpoints and verified by replay). Books II and III, GOV-anchors, LORE, the
Warrant 0.x apparatus and the 0.7.0 gate and review material were retired on
2026-10-31: [history/RETIREMENT-2026-10-ECHO.md](history/RETIREMENT-2026-10-ECHO.md)
says what left, why, and the commit that keeps its bytes.

## Orient yourself first

- **`master` is the only thing in force.** Branches are candidates: readable,
  citable, not adopted. Check the ref before reporting anything absent — that
  single mistake is the source of most false findings filed against this project.
- `.warrant/`: this repository's Warrant 3 records — pull-request heads, reviews,
  findings — read with `warrant status` and `warrant review view` (warrant-graph).
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): conduct rules, and the incident that caused them.

## Check anything in one command

```bash
tools/test-all.sh                               # everything, one verdict
```

A surface that could not be checked (no `lean` on PATH) is named in the verdict
and exits 2, never ALL GREEN. `ALLOW_SKIPS=1` is how you say the gap was
deliberate.

Individual pieces:

```bash
python3 impl/sigma_glyph.py                     # ALL PASS            (Book I)
python3 tests/spec_conformance/run_reference.py # CONFORMANCE: ALL PASS
python3 tests/resume_test.py                    # SIGMA-RESUME: … PASS, 0 FAIL
python3 tools/verify_anchors.py                 # the adopted specification bytes
```

When a document and a command disagree, the command is right.

## The specification

- [spec/book-1-truth.md](spec/book-1-truth.md) — normative. Canonical bytes,
  SHA-256 identity, SKI normal-order reduction, size-priced ATP. The contract two
  independent nodes need to agree on a result hash. `book-1-truth.en.md` is an
  informative translation, not the citation target.
- [spec/sigma-resume.md](spec/sigma-resume.md) —
  normative with Book I (draft standard): segments, checkpoints, resume, receipts.

Two implementations from one author/model lineage agree on all 49 vectors and on
generated terms (Python and Rust), and the evaluator's determinism, totality and
memory bound are machine-checked in Lean 4 (`proofs/`). Bounded by SA-1: part of
that chain rests transitively on `native_decide`, which puts the compiler in the
trusted base as well as the kernel.

## If you are reviewing

Run first, read second. A finding is a reproduction, not a sentence: blocks that
report a violation whatever the machine does have been submitted here by three
separate reviewers.

## Reporting a defect

[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — scope, the reporting channel, and the severity
ladder (P0 = two nodes disagree on a result hash, or a resumed computation
disagrees with a straight run). What is out of scope is a stated boundary of the
threat model, defined once in [SECURITY-ASSUMPTIONS.md](SECURITY-ASSUMPTIONS.md).

## Who holds authority here

Model actors in this project are **delegated, bounded actors under a root of
authority held by a human** — never the maintainer of record, never where
non-repudiation rests. See SA-6.
